# Workflow — Board, Commits & Releases

_Applies when: planning, tracking, committing, or releasing work in any agent-core project (web/api/mobile)._

How work is planned, tracked, and shipped. Tool-agnostic; project specifics
(board paths, agent roles, app names) live in each project's CLAUDE.md.

## Scrum board (`.scrum/`)

- Track each story as a file moved through status folders:
  `backlog/` → `in-progress/` → `review/` → `done/`. Moving the file changes state.
- Domains get their own sub-boards (e.g. `shared/`, `api/`, `web/`, `mobile/`);
  cross-domain dependencies tracked in a `BOARD.md`.
- Story file: YAML-ish header (Domain, Status, Tier, Depends-on) + `## Description`,
  `## Acceptance Criteria` (checklist), `## Reference`. 3+ testable AC per feature.
- `project-standards.md` (tech-stack versions, conventions) is the reference for all agents.

## Effort tiers — match ceremony to size

_"Effort" here is process ceremony / team size, not reasoning effort: model and reasoning effort
stay maximal at every tier (see `06-model-effort`)._

- **Bugfix** (1–2 files): analyze → fix → review. No board epic.
- **Lite** (2–5 files): brief scope → implement → quick QA.
- **Full** (5+ files / multi-layer): plan → parallel implementation → review → acceptance.
- Rule of thumb: don't run full ceremony below ~5 files. See `25-orchestration.md`.

## Commits & branches

- **Conventional Commits** (commitlint-enforced): `feat: fix: docs: chore: refactor:`
  `perf: test: style: ci: build: revert: release:`, scope optional (`feat(web): …`), subject ≤ 100 chars.
- Feature branches: `feat/short-desc`, `fix/short-desc`. One PR per feature/fix.
- Never push to `main` without an explicit go-ahead — especially auto-deploy targets
  (Cloudflare Pages). No `--no-verify`; no destructive git ops without approval.
- SemVer for anything versioned; bump the version with the change.
- The per-project merge/branch/version policy — which merge bumps or tags, and to which branch — must be defined once via the `setup-changelog` skill (default: trunk-based, feature → main). It is a per-project choice, not an org-wide mandate.

## Documentation discipline

- Update `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` on every change — manual commit or agent alike. The reusable changelog/version/branch standard — and where its scaffolding comes from — lives in the `setup-changelog` skill.
- Write an ADR (`docs/decisions/ADR-NNNN-*.md`, MADR format: status/date/context/
  decision/consequences) for every architecture decision — and for adopting ANY new
  dependency or technology (justify it against the canonical stack first).
- Move the story file to `done/` as part of finishing.

## Cutting a release — keep `[Unreleased]` current, release deliberately

- Keep `[Unreleased]` current on **every** change, and commit freely to `main` — both are free.
- A **tagged release** is what triggers CI (publish + bundle + showcase seed) and **costs money**,
  so it is a **deliberate, explicit** step — never reflexive per change. **Batch** related changes
  (especially small patches) and cut **one** release on explicit go-ahead or at a meaningful
  milestone, not a CI run per patch.
- Don't let `[Unreleased]` drift *silently*: when changes are shippable, **flag that a release is
  pending** and let the human decide when to tag. Never tag an outward-facing publish without go-ahead.
- When you do cut: bump per SemVer, move `[Unreleased]` → `[x.y.z] - <date>`, add the footer link,
  commit `release: vx.y.z`, tag — bump and changelog finalized **together**, never one without the other.

## Release order

- When a change spans dependent packages, ship in dependency order:
  **shared-types/contracts → api → web/mobile** — never in parallel.
  Shared Zod types are defined first, API contracts next, then clients.
